subject: how do I reduce the file sizes produced when saving spectro() figures as tiff/pdf/eps?

messages.author: 08d16d5dfbfab388
messages.subject: how do I reduce the file sizes produced when saving spectro() figures as tiff/pdf/eps?
parts:
Hello,
I'm using the spectro() function to produce spectrograms for a publication, however I've noticed that the file sizes produced when I save the R figures as pdf, eps or tiff files are prohibitively large (90+ MB even for tiff files!). Since these are for publication, I can't use lossy compression to reduce the file size - I have to keep a resolution of at least 300 dpi. Does anyone have any tricks or advice about how to reduce the large files produced by spectro() without sacrificing image quality? Thanks!
 
- Brianna

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] how do I reduce the file sizes produced when saving spectro() figures as tiff/pdf/eps?
parts:
Hi Brianna,

This isn't really a Seewave issue, but more of an R issue. Are you using the tiff() function to save your files? I would specify the exact file width and height you need (in inches or cms or what have you) and the dpi/res. I think that should give you a decent file size without being too big...

Let me know how that works for you,

Steffi

parts:
Hi Steffi,
Thanks for your advice - I was using tiff() and specifying a file width/height. 300dpi with a width & height of 1800 px and lossless "lzw" compression produced a 13 MB file, which is a slightly more reasonable size than the 90 MB file I produced earlier (600 dpi with dimensions of 4800 px). But for some reason the 1800 width/height choice appears to have distorted the Amplitude scale bar (makes it very skinny) and cuts off the scale bar label at the top right corner. I'm not sure why that would happen as I'm still inputing square dimensions.  My preference was actually to use .eps because I thought the file size would be much smaller (on the order of KB rather than MB) as this has been my past experience with standard R graphs. But for some reason graphs produced with spectro() and saved as eps are 500+ MB. Any ideas on why this would be the case? PDFs are also big at ~50 MB. Thanks for any help on this!
 
Cheers,
- Brianna

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] how do I reduce the file sizes produced when saving spectro() figures as tiff/pdf/eps?
parts:
Hi Brianna,

I'm not sure exactly. However, I'm pretty sure you shouldn't use both resolution AND define pixel widths... I would define your res = 300, and then use width = 10, height = 10, units = "in" (or whatever you want). That should produce a figure with a resolution of 300 ppi at 10 inches square. The tiff function will calculate what the dimensions in px should be to achieve the widths and height you want, given your resolution.

I'm not 100% sure of the details, but I hope this helps,

messages.author: bfa183f4897a5619
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] how do I reduce the file sizes produced when saving spectro() figures as tiff/pdf/eps?
parts:
Hi Brianna,

I can't add much to what Steffi said, but regarding eps format: that is a vector format, and so it is great for normal line-based R plots. Spectrograms are generally noisy, and are therefore best suited to a pixel-based format such as tiff.

One other lossless pixel-based format possibility which I haven't seen mentioned here would be png - might be worth a try!

best,
jesse

messages.author: de80047cbc18c87e
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] how do I reduce the file sizes produced when saving spectro() figures as tiff/pdf/eps?
parts:
Hi all,

Yes vector format (eps and pdf) should be avoided for a spectrogram. You may need to convince the publisher...

I usually use the png raster format: it is a free, open, light and lossless format.

The following parameters usaully provide nice results:

data(tico)
png("tico.png", width=1200, height=1200, point=20)
spectro(tico, ovlp=85)
dev.off()

png("tico_res300.png", point=12, width=3000, height=3000, res=300)
spectro(tico, ovlp=85)
dev.off()

HTH

Jerome
